title: Premium member return behaviour
statementMd:
Compare tiers: for each tier show total loans, loans returned late, loans still out and the late percentage among returned loans (rounded to 1 decimal).

Expected columns: `tier`, `loans`, `late`, `still_out`, `late_pct`.

Tables: `authors`, `books`, `members`, `loans`.

Row order does not matter.
solutionMd:
```sql
SELECT m.tier, COUNT(*) AS loans, SUM(l.return_date > l.due_date) AS late, SUM(l.return_date IS NULL) AS still_out, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(l.return_date > l.due_date) / SUM(l.return_date IS NOT NULL), 1) AS late_pct FROM loans l JOIN members m ON m.id = l.member_id GROUP BY m.tier;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
